claims.text: The alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
The tested WTaTiVZr material is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The WTaTiVZr alloy can be produced by a non-melting powder-metallurgy or similar route in the stated single-phase condition.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially processed pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially processed pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Chemical complexity in WTaTiVZr produces severe lattice distortion and changes the local energy landscape for dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr lowers the effective Peierls barrier specifically for edge dislocations.
Edge dislocations can play a key role in the high-temperature mechanical response of BCC high-entropy alloys.
The lowered barrier gives edge dislocations in WTaTiVZr greater mobility than dislocations in pure tungsten.
Enhanced edge-dislocation mobility produces more homogeneous plastic deformation.
More homogeneous plastic deformation delays crack initiation.
Under identical testing at temperatures of at least 1000 K, WTaTiVZr will have lower yield strength than pure tungsten.
Under identical testing at temperatures of at least 1000 K, WTaTiVZr will have greater plastic strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical testing at temperatures of at least 1000 K, WTaTiVZr will have greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will exhibit a more distributed network of mobile edge dislocations, fewer localized stress concentrations, and later crack initiation than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten typically has high yield strength but limited plastic strain because of brittleness and inefficient dislocation mobility under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
The proposed mechanism should dominate above tungsten's ductile-brittle transition when dislocation dynamics control plasticity.
The proposed mechanism may not govern at lower temperatures.
Additional phases or precipitates can supersede the proposed dislocation mechanism and govern deformation.
Identical high-temperature tensile, nano-indentation creep, and in situ TEM testing of WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten is proposed as the controlled comparison.

contradictions.description: The initial state and boundary describe a single-phase HEA in which additional phases or precipitates are absent, while the uncertainty field allows secondary precipitates to contribute to the claimed improvement.
